lead: you have not lied to anybody. what you did instead was stop saying the kind of thing that becomes terms when it is said, and forty years of that leaves an interior nobody has visited.
sun: everything you have said in earnest to a person has become a term, and every one of those terms has held. it runs on ordinary sentences — what you would like, where you thought the two of you were going, what you would do if it came to it. spoken to somebody's face, any of those is entered, and entered here means kept for thirty years by a person who no longer wants it.
moon: the wanting went under cover early, and the cover has stood for decades on one support: nobody with the standing to hold you to an answer has put the question in an hour when you would have answered it. that is the whole structure. there is nothing disgraceful under it, only the ordinary contents of a person, kept out of reach of your own faculty for binding yourself.
pull: the contents are ordinary, and they are under there because you cannot say a true thing to somebody's face without it becoming a thirty-year term. the covering stands on nobody having asked.
tension: a covering on one support does not sag first, which decides how this goes when it goes. somebody asks properly, at the right hour, and the interior arrives in one piece — and out of your mouth it arrives as an undertaking, since that is the only form you have for saying a true thing to a person. the disclosure and the commitment turn out to be one sentence, and whoever is in the room receives both.
cost: nothing you have said to a person has needed discounting, in forty years, by anybody, and people organise their decade around that without registering that they are doing it. what it took was the removal of your own case from circulation. the interior has gone on growing the whole time, unvisited, and is now too large to be introduced into an ordinary evening at any speed.

lead: the house is too big and in the wrong town, and nine people's things are in the roof of it. what fixed it there was one sentence, said at twenty-nine, to a person who has moved three times since.
sun: at twenty-nine, in a bad year, the subject was a location. this would be the one thing in the group that stayed put, and anybody could give the address as their own for as long as they needed. it was entered between two adults, level, with nothing enforcing it, and it has never come up for review, so a sentence from a bad year now governs a building neither of you would choose today.
moon: the arrangement conceals nothing. anyone could work out what the mortgage is and who has been carrying it, and the reason no one has is that a room does not prompt the question. your nephew has his post sent here and thinks of the place as geography. what holds it up is standing in plain view, unmentioned, in the way of walls.
pull: your address is geography to nine people. it was a decision, taken once at twenty-nine, and four separate households are standing on it.
tension: you live in two rooms of it. the others are kept made up for people who come twice a year, and the heating goes on in all of them, because a cold room stops being a room. every practical argument has run one way for a decade. the sentence that would put it on the market has not formed in you, and each time somebody's circumstances go wrong the argument resets to nothing.
cost: three separations and one bankruptcy went through that house without anybody having to ask whether it would still be there, and that is the whole return on it. where you live was never your decision. the town was picked by a job you left twenty years ago, and every year since has been spent in it, because leaving would require unsaying something, and unsaying is the one operation missing.

lead: she runs something four times the size of anything you managed, and you still drive over on the second thursday, because of a sentence you said to her at a table when she was twenty-three and had nothing.
sun: she can still quote the evening: whatever this takes, for however long. terms of that shape have no completion clause in them — nothing in the wording described the state of affairs in which the thing would be finished, and no later occasion has arrived on which it could be amended. you were addressing an equal, which she was not yet and is now, and the words have gone on operating at their original size.
moon: carrying somebody across is finite work. The Guide reads a route for another person and stops at the line, and yours stopped on an afternoon you could name — the day she began describing problems you had no equipment to assess. there have been eleven years of visits since, and the advice inside them would not survive being written down. what you bring over now is attendance.
pull: you got her across in four years and you have been going over for eleven more with nothing left to give her, because the words you used had no finishing condition in them.
tension: a release would have to come from her, and she has no standing to give one, since the terms went out from you and she was never asked to agree to anything. so she manages the visits, kindly, the way she manages her staff. you sit in a room that runs itself and answer questions framed to be answerable. neither of you has said that the work finished eleven years ago, and neither of you holds a sentence that would.
cost: nine people are across who had no route in, and each was carried well past the point where it stopped being interesting, since interest was never the thing holding it. the list only accumulates. nothing discharges anybody from it, so the hours available for the next twenty-three-year-old with nothing are whatever is left over from the ones already delivered.

lead: slack is the only adjustment a rope has. nothing in you performs it, so every line you have put out is at working tension this afternoon, all of them, including the ones whose far ends stopped pulling years ago.
sun: an undertaking here has one setting. it is in force, at full value, from the evening it was given, and no version of it exists at half. that suits a rope and suits a person badly, because you have gone on adding lines — the one from your twenties, two from the bad decade, one given last spring on a platform — and no fastening has come off to make room for the next.
moon: a line under tension carries in both directions. a bad fortnight at the far end arrives in your week at full size with no message having been sent, and sympathy has nothing to do with it; the cord simply conducts. you have known which of them is in trouble, and on which afternoon, for thirty years, and been right often enough to stop treating the sensation as a mood.
pull: there has been no unloaded hour in your adult life, so you have never learned what you weigh by yourself, and the only setting the equipment has is taut.
tension: a given week does not separate into yours and theirs. a flat fortnight gets filed as a fault in you, and it usually is one, and also somebody two hundred miles off having a bad month, arriving along the line at identical volume. when a far end does let go — somebody recovers, somebody genuinely stops needing anything — what arrives is not relief. you find yourself driving over to check on people who are well.
cost: several of them have stopped keeping any other line at all, on the evidence that nothing of yours has gone slack from inattention in thirty years. the same fact removes any ability to concentrate. a promise given last spring pulls exactly as hard as one given at twenty-two, so the thing currently going wrong gets the share of a person carrying six that are fine.
